newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius Happy World Foods issues debentures.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius Happy World Foods issues debentures.

text.p: Happy World Foods (HWF) opened on Monday a sale issue of 200 million rupees ($9.72 million) of secured debentures to raise funds for a new ice-cream factory and a modern warehouse complex, HWF Chief Executive Antoine Seeyave said on Monday.

The debentures, with a coupon rate of 10.5 percent per annum, are being sold at their nominal value of 1,000 rupees each in a sale issue to remain open until 9 June 1997, HWF chairman Rene Seeyave said.
Rene Seeyave said HWF debentures have a maturity date up to 8 June 2002, but early redemption of the securities can occur at the discretion of the company after 8 June 2000.

Out of the 200 million rupees on issue, 50 million rupees were earmarked for private placement with local commercial banks and the remaining 150 million rupees were available for public issue, Rene Seeyave said.
The HWF debentures should be quoted on the Stock Exchange of Mauritius in July 1997.
For the financial year ending 30 June 1997, HWF estimate profit before taxation amounted to 85.36 million rupees from 62.59 million rupees one year earlier.
HWF turnover is estimated at one billion rupees for the year ending 1996/97 from 873.94 million rupees in 1995/96.
Antoine Seeyave said the security offered by the company's assets and its earnings potential demonstrate adequate capacity to pay interest and repay capital to debenture holders.

It was necessary to develop measures to encourage the issuance of corporate debentures including the creation of a rating agency to rate all local debt issues, the eligibility of listed debentures for meeting the statutory liquidity requirements of banks and insurance companies and the active development of a government bond market, he said.
